result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers fit the audience well and offer contextual hints, a command palette, a small starter set and rebinding. A grounds its objection more directly in busy lawyers who skip the tour and need to get to real work. It also keeps the guided element down to a first task that uses two or three shortcuts, and gives the PM a clear measurable goal. B proposes an A/B test that could keep the full tour alive and makes the doubtful claim that Westlaw and Outlook users expect a command palette, so it is slightly weaker on rubric items 1 and 4. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both reject the day-one tour and propose a command palette, contextual hints, a small starter set and rebinding. B ties its reasons more closely to busy professionals: the tour delays their first real task. B also adds shortcut labels next to the menu items people already use and gives the PM a clear, measurable goal. A's claim that lawyers expect a command palette from Westlaw and Outlook is doubtful, and its proposed A/B test keeps the full tour alive as an option.
